h1: The 8 Best Samsung TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight Samsung TVs across OLED, Mini-LED, QLED and Crystal UHD, from 43 to 98 inches, matched to room size and budget.
summary: The 65-inch Samsung S90H OLED is the best all-round pick for a main living room. The 55-inch M70H Mini-LED is the sensible step down for a smaller budget, and the 98-inch Q7F QLED is the choice if you want a wall-sized screen.
intro: Samsung sells TVs under panel names that sound alike, so buyers often pay OLED money for a screen they only needed in LED, or buy a huge set for a room that cannot fit it. The panel type and the screen size both matter more than the model number.

We reviewed eight Samsung sets across OLED, Mini-LED, QLED and Crystal UHD families, and ranked them on panel type, size range, price tier and fit for typical rooms. Our source is the listing specs, which give size and panel type only, so we do not claim brightness or feature numbers we cannot confirm.

products.name: Samsung 65-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: OLED at a size that suits most living rooms.
products.description:
The 65-inch S90H is a Samsung OLED, the premium panel family in this guide. Expect to spend over $500.

The top slot goes to it since 65 inches is the most common living room size and OLED is the top panel tier here. Compared with the 55-inch S90H it gives a bigger picture, while the 77-inch costs more and needs a bigger wall.

Buy it for a main TV where picture quality matters most. The caveat is price, so pick the Mini-LED M70H if you want to spend less.
products.idealFor: Main living rooms where picture quality leads.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: Samsung 55-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: The same OLED family in a smaller footprint.
products.description:
The 55-inch S90H is the smaller OLED in Samsung's S90H lineup, and costs $500+.

It places second because the 65-inch version gives a larger picture for the same family, but 55 inches fits bedrooms and tighter living rooms better.

Buy it for a bedroom or small lounge where OLED quality matters. Skip it if your seat is far from the screen.
products.skipIf: You sit far from the screen.

products.name: Samsung 55-Inch Class M70H Series
products.description:
The 55-inch M70H uses a Mini-LED panel and lands in the $200-500 bucket, well under the OLED sets.

It ranks third because it is the cheapest route to a higher-tier panel here, while the OLED S90H models give the premium picture.

Choose it if you want a balanced set without OLED pricing. The listing gives little beyond size and panel, so check other features before buying.

products.name: Samsung 77-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: OLED at 77 inches for a dedicated screen wall.
products.description:
The 77-inch S90H is the largest OLED in this group and costs $500+.

It ranks fourth because it needs a big wall and a large budget, which suits fewer buyers than the 65 inch.

Buy it for a dedicated movie room. Measure your wall and viewing distance first.

products.name: Samsung 75-Inch Class M70H Series
products.verdict: Mini-LED at 75 inches without OLED pricing.
products.description:
The 75-inch M70H is a Mini-LED set priced at $500+.

It ranks fifth since the 77-inch OLED costs more for the premium panel, while this one makes a big screen more affordable.

Choose it for a large living room on a budget. Confirm details beyond size and panel on the listing.
products.idealFor: Big rooms on a mid budget.

products.name: Samsung 65-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.description:
The 65-inch U8000H is a Crystal UHD 4K TV in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks sixth since it sits below the Mini-LED and OLED panels, but gives the same 65-inch size for less.

Buy it for a bedroom or secondary room. Skip it if picture quality is your top priority.

products.name: Samsung 43-Inch Class QLED Q7F Series Samsung Vision AI Smart TV
products.verdict: A compact QLED with Vision AI smart features.
products.description:
The 43-inch Q7F is a QLED with Samsung Vision AI smart features, priced in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks seventh because its small size narrows the audience, but it is the only compact QLED here.

Choose it for a bedroom, dorm or desk setup. Skip it if you want a big living room screen.

products.name: Samsung 98-Inch Class QLED Q7F Series Samsung Vision AI Smart TV
products.verdict: A 98-inch QLED for the biggest wall.
products.description:
The 98-inch Q7F is a QLED with Samsung Vision AI smart features, the largest screen here. Our listing data has no price tier for it.

It ranks last because few rooms fit it and we cannot confirm its price, but nothing else here approaches its size.

Buy it only for a dedicated theater wall. Measure carefully and confirm the price on the listing.

whatMatters.detail: OLED, Mini-LED, QLED and Crystal UHD are different panel technologies. OLED sits at the premium end. Check the panel name in the listing title.
Bigger is not always better. Match size to viewing distance. Measure the wall and seating before buying.
S90H, M70H, Q7F and U8000H signal different tiers. Compare within a series for the same panel family. Look for the series in the title.
Budget sets use simpler panels. Compare buckets to see what you are paying for. Check the listing price on the day.
Vision AI appears on the Q7F listings. Confirm smart features per model. Read the listing bullets.

cards.label: OLED
cards.text: OLED is Samsung's premium panel here, found in the S90H series at 55, 65 and 77 inches.

cards.label: Mini-LED
cards.text: Mini-LED costs less per inch, found in the M70H at 55 and 75 inches.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to Mini-LED unless picture quality is the priority.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 43 to 55 inch screen and a price you accept for a secondary room.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The 43-inch Q7F QLED suits tiny rooms, while the 55-inch M70H and S90H cover larger bedrooms.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Picture quality matters most, which points to the 65-inch S90H OLED.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The set is for a spare room, where the 65-inch U8000H or 55-inch M70H is enough.

faq.q: What is the difference between QLED and OLED?
faq.a: They are different panel technologies. The listings here label the S90H as OLED and the Q7F as QLED, with OLED at the premium end.

faq.q: What mistake do people make buying a big TV?
faq.a: Ignoring wall and seat distance. A 98-inch set needs a lot of space.

faq.q: Is Mini-LED worth it over Crystal UHD?
faq.a: The M70H Mini-LED costs more than the U8000H Crystal UHD at similar sizes, so it is worth it if you value the better panel.

faq.q: How do I set up a new Samsung TV?
faq.a: Mount or place it, connect Wi-Fi and sign in. The Q7F lists Vision AI smart features.

faq.q: How do I maintain the screen?
faq.a: Wipe with a dry microfiber cloth and avoid sprays.

faq.q: Can a 43-inch TV work as a desk monitor?
faq.a: It can fit a desk setup, but check ports and viewing distance first.

finalTake: The 65-inch Samsung S90H OLED is our best all-round pick. Choose the 55-inch M70H for value, and the 98-inch Q7F only for a theater wall.
